title: Lake Weyba

bikeon.heading: Lake Weyba
paras: Lake Weyba is the southern gateway to the Noosa Everglades system: a large, shallow, tidal saltwater lake fringed by mangroves, saltpans and open forest, and linked to the lower Noosa River by Weyba Creek. It is listed in the Directory of Important Wetlands in Australia and is an important fish breeding habitat. Weyba is understood to mean place of stingrays in the Kabi Kabi language. It was once spelt Weiba. For the Kabi Kabi people the lake was a rich source of food, and shell middens and scarred trees remain around its shores. Noosa's first professional fisherman, Joseph Keyser, settled on the north-west shore and is remembered for wheeling smoked mullet to the Gympie goldfields in a barrow. Today the whole eastern shore is national park.

story: Lake Weyba is the southern gateway to the Noosa Everglades system. It is a large, shallow, tidal saltwater lake, fringed by mangroves, salt pans and open forest, and joined to the Noosa River by Weyba Creek.
It is listed as a wetland of national importance, and it is an important breeding ground for fish.

Weyba is understood to mean place of stingrays in the Kabi Kabi language. It was once spelt Weiba. For the Kabi Kabi people the lake was a rich source of food, and shell middens and scarred trees remain around its shores.

Noosa's first professional fisherman, Joseph Keyser, settled on the north west shore, and he is remembered for wheeling smoked mullet all the way to the Gympie goldfields in a barrow. Today the whole eastern shore is national park.
